items.item_text: Medical Assistant Diploma.
Experience working in an environment performing tasks related to front and back office duties related to this position.
Experience using standard exam room medical equipment and computers.
Experience working in a women's health, primary care, or multi-specialty clinic.

Patient Flow: Determining the chief complaint and documenting it in the patient's electronic medical record with close attention to accurate use of medical terms. Interviews patient to obtain medical information and record medical history/information, measure vital signs, weight, and height, and records information in the electronic medical record. Administer appropriate questionnaires, pend orders per protocol to meet quality guidelines and assess social drivers of health(SDOH). Show patients to examination rooms and prepare them for the physician. Assisting with treatments and exams, including but not limited to minor dressing changes; suture removal; staple removal; injections and chaperoning. Explain treatment procedures, medications, diets, or physicians' instructions to patients. Prepare treatment rooms for patient examinations and procedures, keeping the rooms neat and clean and stocked with necessary supplies. Assist in the patient flow and time schedules by assisting physician with cycle times. Prepare for the patient check out process by ensuring orders for follow up lab, radiology, referrals, medication administration record, Rx are entered, and patient has needed after visit summary information. Schedule follow up visits. (45% time)

Monitor and respond to messages in the EMR pool, provider, and personal in-baskets. Answer in-basket messages and prepare charts for upcoming appointments. Maintains patient accounts by obtaining, recording, and updating personal, and compliance information into the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). Assists providers and patients with access and navigation to the patient portal. Monitor and respond to phone messages to address matters not concerned with scheduling. Follow up on messages from answering service for after hours calls. (15% time)

Front Office (Patient Welcome): Provides a warm welcome with appropriate etiquette to patients and visitors by greeting in person or on the telephone and answering or referring inquiries. Educates on the clinic services and the provider’s background. Responds to patients', prospective patients, and visitor inquiries in a courteous manner. Comforts patients by anticipating patients' anxieties; answering patients' questions; maintaining the reception area. Collects co-pays for visits and reconciles deposits. (10% time)

Medication Administration and Prescriptions: Process prior authorization for medication request form and keep detailed, organized record of approvals and/or denials. Prepare and administer medications/vaccines under the supervision of physician or RN. In tandem with physician, authorize drug refills and provide prescription information to pharmacies. (10% time)

Inventory Control and Office Maintenance: Monitor Medical Supplies inventory; consult with supervisor regarding items needed. Maintain the supply room in an orderly fashion, so that supplies are easily located, and storage space is maximized. Monitors office equipment. Maintains business office inventory and equipment by checking stock to determine inventory level; anticipating needed supplies; placing and expediting orders for supplies; verifying receipt of supplies; scheduling equipment service and repairs. Cleaning and Sterilization: Clean and sterilize instruments and dispose of contaminated supplies. Clean exam rooms, workstations, and equipment as necessary. (5% time)
Other duties as assigned, including but not limiting to front office functions. (5% time)

Policies, Protocols, and Procedures: Protects patients' rights by maintaining confidentiality of personal and financial information. Maintains operations by following policies and procedures; reporting needed changes. Protects patient confidentiality by making sure protected health information (PHI) is secured by not leaving PHI in plain sight and logging off the computer before leaving it unattended. (5% time)

Patient Testing. Laboratory Collection and Processing: Perform routine laboratory point of care testing and sample analyses. Collect specimens, log, and prepare for testing. Retrieves lab and test results as needed and uploads to the medical record. Ensures process is followed for physician review. Conducts or assists in office based clinical procedures, assessments, & exams. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Frequently
Write: Frequently
Perform Calculations: Occasionally
Communicate Orally: Frequently
Reason & Analyze: Occasionally
Bend: Occasionally
Sit: Occasionally
Squat: Occasionally
Stand: Frequently
Walk: Frequently

Other: Must be able to lift up to and push / pull 50 pounds. Must be able to assist patients with mobility during rooming patients and in preparation for exams/procedures. Able to respond to assist in emergency scenarios; administer CPR.
Understanding of medical terminology.
Bilingual-English/Spanish.
Must demonstrate customer service skills appropriate to the job.
Familiarity with universal precautions, handling of bio-hazardous waste, specimen identification and transport.
Must possess the skill, knowledge, and ability essential to the successful performance of assigned duties.
Ability to maintain a work pace appropriate to the workload.
Ability to work well in a constantly changing environment.
Strong oral and written communication skills to effectively communicate with patients of varying ages and multicultural backgrounds.
Strong interpersonal skills.
